events.title: PHP Tools 1.0 announced
events.summary: Rasmus Lerdorf announced Personal Home Page Tools (PHP Tools) 1.0 on Usenet — the first release bearing the name PHP.
events.about: PHP started as C CGI binaries for dynamic personal home pages — guestbooks, hit counters, and form handling before databases were standard on the web. It grew into the server-side language behind WordPress, Wikipedia (MediaWiki), Facebook's early stack, and millions of `.php` sites. Today it still powers a large share of the web via Laravel, Symfony, and WordPress.

narrative.whyChosen: PHP made server-side web programming accessible on cheap shared hosting — upload a file, it runs.
narrative.whyImportant: It democratized dynamic websites the way JavaScript later democratized front-end interactivity.
narrative.problemSolved: Static HTML could not handle forms, logs, or counters; Lerdorf needed simple CGI tools without Perl or Tcl on his host.

sources.title: Lerdorf — Announce: Personal Home Page Tools (PHP Tools) v1.0 (Jun 8, 1995)
